The most common win left on "Triple Red 7s Multiplier" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and twelve of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Tomorrow's count on "Triple Red 7s Multiplier" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
802.headline: What's actually left to win

803.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Triple Red 777s", about two-thirds are still unsold. The game is near the midpoint of its run, with three of five top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Tomorrow's count on "Triple Red 777s" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.

805.headline: Tickets sold so far

806.body:
"Win $50, $100 or $200" is in the middle of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

If you play "Win $50, $100 or $200" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

818.headline: How much has sold

819.body:
The key fact about "30X Cash" is how its eight prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

The numbers for "30X Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
